email.subject1: a signal play for dbt Labs
email.body1:
Taylor, saw dbt Labs just merged with Fivetran to build data infrastructure for agents.

A merger that big puts more major accounts in play than the team can cover while the combined motion settles, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for dbt Labs off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Taylor, quick follow-up for dbt Labs.

Post-merger, board expectations on majors pipeline usually jump faster than headcount can. Most teams don't know how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your majors motion needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Taylor, last bit of proof for dbt Labs.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your majors reply rate likely compares to other data-platform teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Taylor, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling majors pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority through the integration, no problem at all. Post-merger stretches are their own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a majors motion? I'll tailor it to dbt Labs either way.
